source.template: QMH Cancer Reporting Template - GI-HCC (Hepatocellular carcinoma)
source.staging: AJCC 8th edition pTNM derived from the number of tumours (satellitosis counts as multiple), the size of the largest tumour, vascular invasion and the tumour-extension ticks (a major branch of the portal or hepatic vein, the visceral peritoneum, the diaphragm or another adjacent organ other than the gallbladder is pT4), the nodal counts and the distant-metastasis options. Complete necrosis after treatment is ypT0. pTNM prints only with the printPTNM option, stamped (AJCC 8th edition).
source.grading: WHO 5th edition digestive system tumours (2019): grade in three tiers on the worst area, with the QMH G1-G4 options; the WHO 5th edition subtypes follow the QMH types in the list.

fields.label: Number of tumours
fields.help: Each separate tumour nodule. Satellite nodules are recorded under Satellitosis; they count as multiple tumours for pT (AJCC 8th edition).

fields.label: Largest tumour: greatest dimension (cm)
fields.help: pT turns on 2 cm (solitary tumour) and 5 cm (multiple tumours), so record the largest tumour in cm. After treatment, give the largest viable tumour: only viable tumour is used for staging (CAP).

fields.label: Tumour histology and immunohistochemical studies (typed text replaces the derived sentence)
fields.placeholder: The tumour cells are positive for HepPar-1 and arginase-1.

fields.label: Histologic type (WHO, as on the QMH page; WHO 5th edition subtypes below the line)
fields.help: WHO 5th edition subtypes (RCPath Appendix N): steatohepatitic (more than 50% of the tumour), clear cell (more than 80% clear cells), macrotrabecular-massive (more than 50% of the tumour in trabeculae 10 or more cells thick), scirrhous (more than 50% dense fibrosis), chromophobe, fibrolamellar, neutrophil-rich and lymphocyte-rich. Combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma is staged with the intrahepatic bile duct protocol.

reference.title: HCC subtypes
reference.intro: The predominant subtype informs the diagnosis; clear cell needs more than 80% and steatohepatitic 50% (ICCR). Definitions from RCPath Appendix N (after WHO).

groups.heading: Steatohepatitic
points: More than 50% of the tumour: steatotic and ballooned tumour cells, Mallory-Denk bodies, inflammation and pericellular fibrosis

images.caption: Steatohepatitic HCC: multinodular yellow-grey mass (a); tumour cells with fat droplets and ballooning (b, H&E x100), positive for HepPar-1 (c).

groups.heading: Clear cell
points: More than 80% of the tumour with clear cells from glycogen; steatotic cells may be present
Torbenson recommends at least 50%: the sources differ

images.caption: Clear cell HCC in a cirrhotic liver: grey nodular tumour (a), nests of tumour cells (b, H&E x10) with abundant clear cytoplasm (c, H&E x100).

groups.heading: Macrotrabecular-massive
points: More than 50% of the tumour in trabeculae 10 or more cells thick (RCPath); other studies use more than 6
Often with satellite nodules and vascular invasion

images.caption: Macrotrabecular-massive HCC: expanding tumour (a); trabeculae of more than 10 cells surrounded by vascular spaces (b, H&E x100); CD34 shows vessels encapsulating tumour clusters (c).

groups.heading: Lymphocyte-rich
points: Dense lymphoid infiltrate; lymphocytes outnumber tumour cells in most areas
Torbenson: diffuse, in over 50% of the tumour

images.caption: Lymphocyte-rich HCC: circumscribed tumour (a); tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes outnumber the tumour cells (b, H&E x100), which are positive for HepPar-1 (c).

groups.heading: Chromophobe
points: Light or clear cytoplasm; generally mild atypia with focal marked (abrupt) anaplasia
Scattered microscopic pseudocysts

images.caption: Chromophobe HCC: tumour cells with smooth clear cytoplasm and distinct cell membranes (arrows) (H&E).

groups.heading: Fibrolamellar
points: Large eosinophilic cells with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli; pale and hyaline bodies
Dense lamellar fibrosis; non-cirrhotic liver
CK7 and CD68 positive in nearly all cases, but not specific (CAP)

images.caption: Fibrolamellar carcinoma: lobulated tumour with a central scar (a); large polygonal cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli (b, H&E x100); fibrosis in parallel bands (c, Masson trichrome).

groups.heading: Scirrhous and neutrophil-rich
points: Scirrhous: more than 50% of the tumour with dense fibrosis
Neutrophil-rich: numerous neutrophils diffusely infiltrating the tumour; may have sarcomatoid areas

fields.label: Histologic grade
fields.help: CAP (AJCC 8th edition, four tiers): well differentiated tumours closely resemble normal liver; moderately differentiated tumours have thick plates and more prominent reticulin loss; poorly differentiated tumours show marked atypia or high mitotic activity; undifferentiated is rarely used. For multiple tumours, select the worst grade. Not printed for fibrolamellar carcinoma.

reference.title: Grade (CAP, AJCC 8th)
reference.intro: Four tiers, graded on the worst area; for multiple tumours, the worst grade (CAP). ICCR, RCPath and WHO use three, combining Edmondson-Steiner grades 1 and 2 as well differentiated.

groups.heading: G1 Well differentiated
points: Closely resembles normal liver: minimal to mild atypia, relatively thin plates, limited reticulin loss

images.caption: Well-differentiated HCC: trabecular and pseudoglandular growth with mild atypia and bile pigment in the lumina (H&E, x400).
images.credit: Limaiem, Int J Surg Case Rep 2025, Fig 5

groups.heading: G2 Moderately differentiated
points: Thick plates, mild to moderate nuclear atypia and more prominent reticulin loss

images.caption: Moderately differentiated HCC on a liver biopsy: pleomorphic hepatocytes with granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli (H&E, x400).

groups.heading: G3 Poorly differentiated
points: Marked nuclear atypia and/or high mitotic activity; the hepatocellular nature may not be evident

images.caption: Poorly differentiated HCC on a liver biopsy: sheets of markedly atypical cells with multinucleated giant cells and necrosis (H&E).

groups.heading: G4 Undifferentiated
points: Rarely used: no hepatocellular or other differentiation on morphology or immunohistochemistry
CAP: better classed as undifferentiated carcinoma than as HCC

fields.label: Tumour extension (tick every applicable box)
options: Tumour involves a major branch of the portal vein
Tumour directly invades other adjacent organs (specify)

showIf.is: Tumour directly invades other adjacent organs (specify)

reference.title: Satellitosis
reference.intro: Satellite nodules count as multiple tumours for pT (CAP, ICCR, RCPath).

groups.heading: Satellite nodules
points: CAP: an HCC nodule smaller than the primary, within 2 cm of it and separated by non-tumorous liver
WHO, ICCR and RCPath: often multiple, usually within 2 cm of the main tumour
Tumour within a vessel is vascular invasion, not satellitosis (CAP)

images.caption: Encapsulated 4 x 4 cm chromophobe HCC with numerous satellite nodules (blue arrows), each under 2 cm and within 2 cm of the main tumour.
images.credit: Ben-Slama, Arq Bras Cir Dig 2025, Fig 2

groups.heading: Attached co-nodules
points: A co-nodule attached to the main tumour makes a single tumour: an irregular leading edge (ICCR)

images.caption: Gross patterns of HCC: pseudocapsulated nodule in cirrhosis (a); diffuse HCC with multiple satellite nodules (b); infiltrative HCC (c); pseudocapsulated nodule in non-cirrhotic liver (d); macroscopic bile duct invasion (e) and vascular invasion (f), in blue boxes.
images.credit: Sweed, World J Surg Oncol 2022, Fig 2

fields.label: Vascular invasion
options: Present, large vessel invasion (major branch of hepatic vein or portal vein)
fields.help: Small vessel (microvascular) invasion is seen only microscopically; large vessel invasion is of a major branch of the portal or hepatic vein (pT4).

reference.title: Vascular invasion
reference.intro: Vascular invasion is part of T for the liver; a major branch of the portal or hepatic vein is pT4.

groups.heading: Microscopic (small vessel)
points: Tumour in an endothelium-lined space, seen only microscopically, in the capsule, fibrous septa or surrounding liver (CAP)
Attachment to the vessel wall, or smooth muscle or elastic lamina, helps confirm it
Suspicious but short of these criteria: indeterminate (ICCR), not counted for staging

groups.heading: Large vessel (macroscopic)
points: Right or left portal vein, or the right, middle or left hepatic vein: pT4 (RCPath)
CAP also counts the right or left hepatic artery as major vascular invasion
Report a portal vein tumour thrombus (CAP)

fields.label: Vascular invasion: the tumour nodule (if applicable)

reference.title: Treatment effect
reference.intro: No necrosis cut-off has been validated (CAP, ICCR); give the extent of necrosis for up to the five largest nodules.

groups.heading: Complete necrosis
points: Sample a tumour up to 2 cm entirely, plus a section for each further 1 cm (CAP)
Only the size of viable tumour is used for staging (CAP)

images.caption: HCC after balloon-occluded TACE: a totally necrotic tumour (asterisk) with necrotic surrounding parenchyma (c), and complete necrosis of the tumour and peritumoral liver on H&E (d, x10).

groups.heading: Incomplete or no necrosis
points: Incomplete: viable tumour present; give the percentage of necrosis
ICCR uses response terms: complete, partial or no response
